summary: Index/README for a set of four PlantUML C4 diagrams, labelling them as a PROPOSAL to be treated as non-authoritative until PO/ARB acceptance.
contribution_assessment: States explicitly that the four diagrams are a proposal, not accepted architecture, and describes the fourth diagram as a non-classical C4 view for the L3-L5 contract-neutrality boundary.

summary: C4 System Context diagram modelling six Person actors (PO/ARB, Governance Engineer, Governance Communication, Architecture Engineer, Implementation Engineer, Independent Verification Engineer) around a KnowledgeOS system, plus an external repository and AI runtime.
contribution_assessment: This untracked diagram becomes the single most contested piece of evidence in the batch: later verification passes (S0089, S0090) discover it models the six 'Engineer' titles as actual Person() actors with relationships, directly falsifying an early claim that those titles appear 'nowhere' in the architecture.

summary: C4 component diagram of the KOS-CONTRACT-NEUTRALITY-001 pipeline: Source Language -> Language Binding/Extraction -> L3 Fact Model -> L4 Cohesion Semantics -> L5 Metric (LCOM4) -> Conformance Evidence, with two explicit warnings against inference shortcuts.
contribution_assessment: Defines the L0-L5 layered pipeline for the (separate) Track-1 PHP LCOM4 contract-neutrality work and states two structural warnings: qualifier kind must be preserved not inferred from the final metric, and the metric alone is insufficient without the node/edge set.

summary: C4 component diagram of the KnowledgeOS Platform: Composition Root, Session Manager, Workflow Engine, Knowledge Manager, Verification Engine, Review Engine, Drafting Studio, Platform Registry, and a Communication Capability, all persisting into one Knowledge+Workflow Store.
contribution_assessment: Proposes a component-level decomposition of the platform including a distinct 'Communication Capability' component responsible for next-actor instructions, handovers and decision summaries -- an early architectural placement of the communication concern that later capability analysis (S0102) revisits and largely reclassifies as a stewardship rather than a component.

summary: C4 container diagram collapsing the engineering side into a single 'Engineering Roles' Person actor (Governance, Communication, Architecture, Implementation, Verification) alongside PO/ARB, and defining containers: Governance Engine, Communication Capability, Knowledge Engineering, Architecture Workbench, Implementation Workbench, Verification Engine, Session Orchestration, Platform Registry, and one Knowledge/Workflow Estate store.
contribution_assessment: Later verification (S0090) finds this diagram CONTRADICTS 01-system-context.puml on actor decomposition: one collapses the engineering side into a single Person, the other into five separate Persons, and neither contains a distinct Knowledge Engineer actor.

summary: Governance registration authorizing two parallel engineering tracks (Track 1: bounded PHP LCOM4 implementation; Track 2: ADR-AIP-04 capability/role discovery and platform evolution), with a coupling rule that neither track may silently change the shared L3 contract or accepted semantic decisions.
contribution_assessment: Establishes the load-bearing coupling rule that governs the rest of the batch's Track-2 work: any shared-boundary change requires a separate Architecture/PO/ARB act, and recommends ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery be commissioned first among Track 2's four purposes.

summary: The formal commission for ADR-AIP-04: determine capabilities required for a sustainable session-based AI Engineering Operating System before formalizing or extending the role model; declares the six proposed responsibilities as hypotheses, not decisions.
contribution_assessment: Sets the entire discovery's method (capability-first ordering), scope (eight investigations), evidence base, classification discipline (OBSERVED/INFERRED/PROPOSED/DECIDED/OPEN), the boundary rule against silently modifying shared architecture, and the seventeen-section deliverable structure that all later ADR-AIP-04 artifacts follow.

summary: Independent Verification #1 of the ADR-AIP-04 discovery proposal: falsifies two material claims (F-3 six-role 'nowhere', C-14 'absent') using the untracked 01-system-context.puml and registry.yaml AST-007, and returns the proposal for material correction.
contribution_assessment: Introduces the falsification method used throughout the batch, discovers the discovery proposal's evidence-search was truncated (a recurring root-cause pattern), distinguishes non-registration from non-existence, and records a self-declared conflict on SB-1 because the verifier is Track-1's own implementation engineer.

summary: Independent Verification #2, checking Amendment 1's corrections: confirms the withdrawal of F-3 but falsifies Amendment 1's own supporting claim (W-1) that untracked material depicts only a 'five-actor sketch' -- a 925-line brainstorming document actually sets out all six roles and pre-frames ADR-AIP-04's own options.
contribution_assessment: Discovers the same truncated-search failure mode recurring at a wider scope; establishes that SB-1 has now been left uncleared by two consecutive verifications for the same structural reason (both verifiers hold Track-1 authorship); records provenance defects (Amendment 1 declares no producing process) and a lifecycle-record anomaly (the architecture lane handed off but never returned to ACTIVE).

summary: The core ADR-AIP-04 Capability Discovery Proposal (875 lines): a 20-capability inventory, 11 findings (F-1..F-11), an ownership map, ubiquitous-language collisions, an invariant map showing BC-7's invariants are mechanically enforced while nearly everything else is declared-only, a role/stewardship analysis of the six hypotheses, and shared-boundary risks (SB-1/2/3) -- followed by Amendment 1 (material corrections after Verification #1) and Correction #2 (further corrections after Verification #2).
contribution_assessment: This is the single richest theoretical artifact in the batch: it identifies four unowned capabilities (C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19) as ADR-AIP-04's real substance rather than the six roles; states the core structural finding that BC-7's invariants are mechanically enforced while everything outside BC-7 is declared-only; proposes (then twice corrects) the six-role finding; and undergoes two rounds of self-correction (Amendment 1, Correction #2) driven by the same root-cause failure mode -- absence-in-a-truncated-search read as absence-of-existence -- recurring three times.

in_file_overlap_claim.target: Amendment 1 explicitly extends/corrects the original proposal; Correction #2 explicitly extends/corrects Amendment 1; both state 'nothing above is rewritten'.

summary: Independent Verification #3 clears SB-1 for the first time by resolving a Track-1 verification report's authorship via write-class tool_use provenance rather than self-declaration, and declares the discovery/Amendment/Correction package READY FOR PO/ARB DECISION with two low-severity residuals.
contribution_assessment: Introduces the write-class tool_use provenance method as a materially stronger evidence class than self-declaration, uses it to establish that a commit hash previously treated as an unnameable exclusion is actually a process already barred, and demonstrates the observation-point mechanism (replacing fixed counts with a stated measurement time) working correctly on first independent test.

summary: PO/ARB decision registration: the six-role model (Governance, Architecture, Implementation, Verification, Knowledge, Communication Engineer) is ADOPTED as the AI Engineering Platform's engineering operating model, explicitly without deciding that any role equals a bounded context, capability, agent, service, or organizational position.
contribution_assessment: This is the pivotal governance decision of the batch: it resolves the six-role hypothesis question (adopted as operating model) while explicitly forbidding the inference that adoption proves any underlying capability or bounded context exists -- a distinction that reframes, but does not moot, all subsequent C-5/C-10/C-14/C-19 capability analysis.

summary: Governance registration of Verification #3's assignment, disclosing that one of the seven barred roles has no session identifier and can only be checked by artifact self-authorship, followed by an appended amendment re-scoping the verification charge after the six-role adoption decision.
contribution_assessment: Documents the delivery/record gap pattern (a lane completes work but its lane never hands off on the record) recurring, and formalises the requirement that the SB-1 independence bar be checked by artifact authorship rather than process hash where an identifier is absent.

summary: A PO/ARB decision pack and subsequent Governance dispositions covering three governance-record integrity questions: a missing workflow START, deleted append-only session-log lines, and a replaced (not amended) decisions register -- ending with the missing START transcribed and the workflow chain unblocked.
contribution_assessment: Demonstrates the estate's own governance discipline in action on itself: Governance refuses to invent or back-date a human act it cannot evidence, distinguishes restoring append-only history (itself a history edit) from recording a truncation with a recovery pointer, and ultimately discharges the gate only once the PO/ARB explicitly affirms the human act occurred.

summary: PO/ARB amendment (AMD2) requiring the just-delivered Capability Architecture Analysis to separate capability EXISTENCE from capability CATEGORY for each of C-5/C-10/C-14/C-19, and to distinguish semantic, evidence, and implementation dependency kinds.
contribution_assessment: Introduces the durable methodological refinement that recurs through the rest of the batch: existence and category are two distinct questions with four admissible existence values (YES, NO, CONTESTED, NOT YET ESTABLISHED), and 'absence of a bounded-context-owned aggregate' must never be read as proof a capability does not exist.

summary: Governance registration of the independent-verification assignment for the AMD2-amended Capability Architecture Analysis, with a charge that verification must check not only correctness of the AMD1/AMD2 corrections but also whether the analysis remains decision-preparation rather than a silent architectural decision.
contribution_assessment: Restates the estate's evidentiary discipline that an uncited/unregistered review cannot be treated as evidence, and formalises 'Verification identifies insufficiency; it does not provide the replacement architecture' as an explicit boundary written into the execution context verbatim.

summary: Brainstorming transcript (apparently a copy of a chat with an external advisory persona, 'ARB Chief / Principal DDD Architect') proposing a FIVE-responsibility operational model (Governance, Architecture, Implementation, Independent Verification, Governance Communication) distinct from the workflow state machine, plus a master strategic sequence ending in ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery.
contribution_assessment: Records an earlier five-responsibility framing (no separate Knowledge Engineer) that predates and is distinct from the six-role model formalized later in the batch; separates the 'role model' (who may act) from the 'workflow state machine' (what happens and in what order), and lists five remaining lifecycle gaps including 'ADR-AIP-04: what capabilities should the AI Engineering Platform formally provide?' as future work.

summary: A verification attempt stops at three independent gates (the assignment does not exist in the record, Correction #3 has not been produced, and this process is the barred 2da45a86), and along the way mechanically falsifies an earlier same-day 'CORRECTION 1' that had claimed the original refusal's identity was false.
contribution_assessment: Introduces the open question of whether a context-compaction continuation of a barred process is itself barred, using write-class create-vs-append and UTC/local timezone reconciliation to re-establish which session actually wrote which artifact -- a second occurrence of the identity-misattribution failure, this time in the opposite (false-bar) direction.

summary: A process refuses a verification assignment on an explicit by-name independence bar; a same-day CORRECTION 1 (by a different, compacted-continuation session) withdraws the refusal's identity claim as false; a subsequent ERRATUM (by the same continuation session) reverses CORRECTION 1, confirming the original refusal's identity claim was true after all.
contribution_assessment: This is the fullest single-file record of the identity-attestation saga: it demonstrates both a false-bar failure (a qualified process wrongly believing itself barred) and documents that root cause as identity inferred from context rather than read from the runtime -- explicitly analogised to C-5 (separation attestation) failing in production on the very work item studying it.

in_file_overlap_claim.target: CORRECTION 1 extends/corrects the original refusal; the ERRATUM extends/corrects CORRECTION 1; both marked additive, nothing rewritten.

summary: The actual independent verification of the AMD2-amended Capability Architecture Analysis: ten of fourteen areas pass, four pass-with-notes, none fail; returns the analysis for correction narrowly on two undischarged mandates (OQ-L's missing definitions of 'constrain' and 'machine-generated result'; a stale executive summary still showing withdrawn verdicts).
contribution_assessment: Confirms, via independent re-derivation from primary sources, that the existence/category separation was correctly applied to all four capabilities without a forbidden collapse; documents its own standing erratum (a compacted-continuation independence defect) rather than concealing it; and finds the six-role adoption's non-equivalence clause held even where all four role->capability pairings remain OPEN.

summary: The canonical Capability Architecture Analysis (922 lines): a 26-point framework applied to C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 individually plus cross-capability analysis, followed by Amendment 1 (existence/category separation applied rigorously) and Correction #3 (repairs the executive surface and the OQ-L definitions per Verification's F-1/F-2).
contribution_assessment: This is the definitive theoretical artifact for the four capabilities: it reframes them as one control loop rather than four candidate contexts, identifies a unifying control-plane invariant candidate (a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party it constrains), tests all four against the six-role forbidden pairings (all remain OPEN), and after two rounds of correction produces the definitive C-5=YES/control-plane, C-10=NOT YET ESTABLISHED, C-14=CONTESTED, C-19=YES/stewardship existence-category matrix.

in_file_overlap_claim.target: Amendment 1 extends the original 26-point analysis; Correction #3 extends/corrects Amendment 1 per Verification findings F-1..F-7; nothing in the chain is deleted.

summary: Governance registration of Correction #3's verification assignment, refused at first because a HANDOFF from a lane that was delivered-but-never-STARTed is mechanically illegal (Inv C); the PO/ARB then transcribes the missing human START and Governance performs the resulting legal handoff.
contribution_assessment: Sharpens the independence-gate vocabulary to seven explicit criteria (including 'not a continuation/compaction/fork/resume lineage of a barred producer' and 'does not inherit material working context') and states the binding sequencing rule that unestablished lineage must classify as NOT ATTESTED, never PASS by default.

summary: A verification attempt on Correction #3 fails the seven-criteria independence gate on four of seven criteria (it IS the barred producer 5e1dd9ee of the original analysis), refuses before opening the artifact, and reports two findings: the grant's own attribution of Correction #3 to this process may itself be wrong, and identity attribution has now failed twice in one day in opposite directions.
contribution_assessment: Demonstrates the pre-substantive gate discipline in practice: identity and provenance metadata are read before the substantive artifact, deliberately preserving the order so a disqualified process cannot un-form views it should never have formed; explicitly analogises the day's repeated identity failures to C-5 (separation attestation) failing in production on the very work item studying it.

summary: Governance provenance reconciliation using write-class tool-use provenance (never grant text, self-declaration, filenames, or prior summaries) to correct the record: Correction #3 was actually produced by claude-code-session:4858c37c, not the grant-attributed 5e1dd9ee, and the same process (4858c37c) authored both the verification findings (F-1..F-7) and the correction answering them -- a defect that requires PO/ARB disposition, not mere reassignment.
contribution_assessment: Formalises the evidence-quality vocabulary AUTHORED / OBSERVED / ASSERTED / NOT ATTESTED and explicitly declares git commit metadata non-probative of process authorship (since every commit carries the same human co-author trailer); this is the single clearest statement in the batch that 'one process on both sides of a governed separation' is itself C-5's subject matter recurring structurally, not incidentally.

summary: Governance refuses a commission to write a fresh C-5 analysis, on two grounds: a canonical analysis already exists and covers all fifteen requested deliverables (ES-005.4 forbids a second), and Governance itself is the wrong actor because it governs the very record C-5 would be analysing.
contribution_assessment: A direct, self-referential demonstration of the canonical-discovery-before-modelling principle (ES-005.4): the refusal itself is offered as C-5 evidence, since refusing to be both governor of the record and author of the analysis resting on it is exactly what separation-attestation-in-practice looks like.

summary: PO/ARB act, recorded by the very process (4858c37c) that is its subject: amends seq-21's producer attribution additively, classifies the verification report (ca6039a8) as HISTORICAL VERIFICATION EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT / PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED and Correction #3 (c3839624) as HISTORICAL CORRECTION ARTIFACT / INDEPENDENTLY UNVERIFIED, and finds that no known process in the estate currently satisfies the seven-criteria verification gate.
contribution_assessment: Introduces the vocabulary for classifying a defective-provenance artifact without deleting or rewriting it: content can be independently assessable while authority and provenance are separately unestablished; explicitly records that content-substance survives as 'unverified' evidence, distinct from the question of who is accountable for it under what authority.

summary: A recording process declines to select among three receipt-authority options (A/B/C) for C-10's OQ-J, reasoning that selecting is the PO/ARB's decision itself; also finds Option C as drafted is unsatisfiable because it binds the receipt to an applicability decision the estate never performs and nobody owns.
contribution_assessment: States a decision-authority boundary distinct from an independence-gate refusal: recording a decision is not the same act as making it, and a process supplying a selection on the PO/ARB's behalf would itself be making the decision.

summary: Records C-10 Decision 1 as DECIDED, Option C (authoritative delivery/acknowledgement only, referencing but not vouching for an applicability decision), corrects a misattribution of the selection to the recording process, and identifies that the decision as worded is not presently populatable because its required applicability-reference points to an act (ContextSelected) with no owner.
contribution_assessment: Introduces the core distinction 'reference != correctness' resolving the earlier OQ-J authority defect, while surfacing a sharper 'referent gap' (the reference points at something that does not exist) that the authority fix alone cannot close; also states the standing rule that untracked external corroborative research may never be cited as authority for a DECIDED act.

in_file_overlap_claim.target: an appended 'AUTHORITATIVE DECISION TEXT' section supersedes the earlier draft's wording within this same file.

summary: A second PO/ARB act addresses the same D1 slot with a materially different proposition (dropping 'knowledge versions K' and the applicability clause), producing a conflict between two undisposed decision texts on the same decision slot; records that Act B's wording would close the referent gap but that a later act arriving is not automatically a supersession.
contribution_assessment: Names the general governance risk that acts and records can cross (now four occurrences within one work item) and establishes the rule that a later act is not automatically read as superseding an earlier DECIDED text absent explicit disposition.

summary: Governance decision-prep for C-10 Decision 2 (capability existence): applies the canonical analysis's ten DDD existence questions and recommends YES, on the ground that D1 (a decided claim-boundary semantic) presupposes a subject -- a recommendation the PO/ARB later rejects.
contribution_assessment: Contains the only recommendation in the batch that the PO/ARB explicitly overrules on methodological grounds (see S0120 D2), making this file's error itself a load-bearing later lesson about conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

summary: Governance decision-prep for C-10 Decision 3 (authoritative state and lifecycle): finds Option B unsound because it would place identity binding inside C-10's authoritative state, which no capability in the estate can establish; recommends Option C (SPLIT) with an explicit non-constitutive clause so the decision does not silently move D2 (existence) by the back door.
contribution_assessment: Names the risk of a 'back-door existence decision' precisely: deciding a capability's boundary constitutively (as if it already existed) would satisfy the adopted-invariant limb of the existence test without ever deciding existence -- and proposes the corrective non-constitutive framing that the eventual D3 decision (S0120) adopts almost verbatim.

summary: Governance decision-prep for D4 (missing/disputed knowledge behaviour): argues any enforcing response would decide C-10's category by consequence, that three of five conditions (stale, superseded, invalidated) have no owner or detectable state, and that since C-10 is NOT YET ESTABLISHED zero receipts exist, so 'Missing' is currently 100% of all cases -- making any blocking response total rather than selective.
contribution_assessment: Provides the decisive practical-arithmetic argument (100% Missing) that later shapes the D4/D4.1 decisions' conservative floor; distinguishes a compensating control as an exception mechanism rather than a fifth enforcement tier, and reframes the estate's own recorded human START acts as a real, already-in-production instance of a compensating control.

summary: Governance-proposed definitions of C-10's five condition types (MISSING, STALE, SUPERSEDED, INVALIDATED, DISPUTED), subdividing MISSING into five sub-conditions (M1-M5) each with a different owner, and establishing that DISPUTED is orthogonal to the lifecycle rather than a terminal state within it.
contribution_assessment: Two structural findings anchor this file: a receipt's D1 claim is a time-stamped historical fact that never becomes false (only insufficient or unrelied-upon), and M4 (a receipt present but unbindable to its execution) must be classified NOT ATTESTED and never MISSING -- extending the NOT-ATTESTED-never-PASS rule to condition-classification level.

summary: Governance-proposed condition-to-response mapping for C-10: every condition and sub-condition results in 'NO ENFORCEMENT RESPONSE YET' because none satisfies all four required prerequisites (semantically defined, authoritative trigger, identifiable evidence source, currently detectable) -- SUPERSEDED comes closest (authority exists at BC-1) but its mechanism (CAP-03) is not built.
contribution_assessment: Demonstrates a rigorous non-enforcement conclusion reached by exhaustively testing each of nine condition rows against four prerequisites; explicitly reasons that DISPUTED cannot be adopted as a suspending effect without deciding who may raise a dispute, since raising a dispute requires far less evidence than resolving one -- a denial-of-service risk.

summary: Governance registers the commission for C-10 Decision 5 (Establishment Criteria: minimum evidence sufficient to move C-10 from NOT YET ESTABLISHED to ESTABLISHED), routed to Architecture rather than authored by Governance itself to avoid concentrating authorship and registration of the same threshold-defining act; three amendments progressively add a Class C (future/architectural, non-establishing) evidence category, a five-axis analysis requirement, and a mandated seven-section artifact structure.
contribution_assessment: Formalises Class C evidence ('future/architectural' items -- proposed schemas, planned stores, an adopted-but-never-exercised invariant -- that must not establish existence by themselves), which retroactively reclassifies D1 itself as advancing C-10's establishment by zero; flags a genuine model-integrity question (are GOVERNED/OBSERVED/REPRODUCIBLE/INDEPENDENT one scheme or several conflated ones?) for the eventual proposal to resolve rather than assuming.

summary: The delivered D5 Architecture proposal: reconciles three evidence schemes into four orthogonal dimensions (Subject, Epistemic, Provenance, Reproducibility), explicitly refuses to add INDEPENDENT as a dimension (it is C-5's subject, not C-10's), defines criteria E1-E10 with full fields, and recommends assurance-level Option C (L1 prototype / L2 operational / L3 authoritative) with D2 flipping only at L2, plus a self-evidencing four-field D2 revisit trigger.
contribution_assessment: Contains the batch's clearest applied instance of model-integrity discipline (testing REPRODUCIBLE and INDEPENDENT separately against orthogonal/necessary/sufficient and accepting only one), and a decisive impossibility proof that a fully-conjunctive Option A test (E1..E10) would make C-10 permanently unestablishable because E10 requires a history that cannot exist at establishment time.

summary: Registers a third PO/ARB act on the D1 slot, reframing it as 'receipt claim boundary stabilization' with an anti-corruption rule (reference != ownership, recording != asserting, correlation != authority) and a new 'external correlation reference' term, while finding it still carries no selection and that the term 'Option C' now denotes two incompatible propositions across the three acts.
contribution_assessment: Names a concrete ubiquitous-language hygiene defect (S-1: the label 'Option C' has crossed meanings across two acts, making 'adopt Option C' unresolvable on the record) and recommends that any future selection be recorded by full proposition text, never by letter -- a rule the eventual final D1 consolidation (S0120) adopts.

summary: Governance decision-prep consolidating the three D1 acts, recommending Proposition 3 (optional, non-authoritative external correlation references) as the only proposition that closes the referent gap without contradicting D3.2, and correcting an earlier claim (that no D5 artifact exists) which had been superseded by events since the delivery of the D5 proposal (S0117).
contribution_assessment: Demonstrates the structural insight that the referent gap is caused by the applicability reference being REQUIRED rather than merely recorded, so making it OPTIONAL dissolves the gap while preserving traceability -- and correctly self-corrects a stale finding rather than letting it stand as if still current.

summary: The single, append-only C-10 decision register: D2 (NOT YET ESTABLISHED, overruling Governance's own YES recommendation), D3 (Option C/SPLIT with a critical non-constitutive clause), D4.1 (risk/context-proportionate enforcement principle, INFO/WARN/BLOCK/HALT+ESCALATE vocabulary), D4 (target principle only, floor WARN+RECORD, no enforcement enabled), D4.3 (partially decided -- only M4=NOT ATTESTED), D5 (framework adopted but criteria undefined in the estate, then AMD1 correcting the status to 'framework adopted, Architecture artifact pending'), and finally D1 (final consolidation, selecting the claims-not-proof wording).
contribution_assessment: This is the definitive record of how C-10 is actually decided across the batch: it documents Governance correcting its own prior recommendation on methodological grounds, twice refuses to let an enforcement decision silently decide category by consequence, and repeatedly demonstrates a 'never launder NOT ATTESTED into PASS/PROVEN' rule recurring across four independent decision surfaces.

in_file_overlap_claim.target: each appended decision (D3, D4.1, D4, D4.3, D5, D5-AMD1, D1-final) explicitly states it is appended to the single register and does not rewrite what precedes it.

summary: Governance disposition of the Correction #3 verification path's provenance defects: attributes Correction #3 to 4858c37c (not the grant-recorded 5e1dd9ee), classifies ca6039a8 as HISTORICAL/NOT INDEPENDENT and the S5 refusal as VALID, and names the four-process barred set for the fresh verifier -- followed by an appended section H clarifying that S5's later HANDED_OFF state means ownership released, not verification performed.
contribution_assessment: Sharpens the distinction between a workflow-engine state transition's mechanical meaning (HANDED_OFF = ownership released) and its human-readable implication (which could wrongly suggest the underlying work concluded) -- explicitly correcting Governance's own earlier overstated claim that no new lane could be made reachable while S5 held ownership.
